newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Late selling takes some shine off Australian bonds.
newsitem.headline: Late selling takes some shine off Australian bonds.

text.p: *Australian bonds ease into close, paring gains held for most of the day in a quiet market held to narrow ranges.
*Market seen well-supported in lead up to next week's second quarter inflation and wage data, waiting for leads from U.S.
Late profit-taking saw Australian bonds weaken to finish flat to slightly weaker across the curve, after spending the bulk of a lacklustre day held to narrow ranges in firmer territory.

Bonds had opened stronger on the back of a firmer U.S. market, and continued to nudge ahead in thin morning trade. In the last hour of trading, however, they eased to their lows, most notably at the short end.
There is little in the way of local data until next week's second quarter inflation and wages data, which are expected to be bond-friendly, so attention is focussed on the U.S. market.
"I think most people's expectations on CPI and wages are very supportive of the market, so a lot will depend on which way the U.S. goes over the course of the week," one trader said.
The key U.S. data in the first half of the week is June retail trade on Tuesday, and Wednesday's June consumer price data will also be watched, traders said.
If the U.S. data disappoints, local bonds are likely to outperform, given the expectations of a near-term rate cut.
"Certainly, if the U.S. starts to sell off we'll probably be fairly well-supported on the way back down, given the good economic fundamentals out there," the trader said.
Manufacturing output prices rose 0.2 percent rise in May, and a 0.8 percent over the year, which economists said reflected an absence of price pressures in the sector.
Late weakness reverses the narrowing held most of the day, though the curve recoups some of last week's steepening.
